Results are `ORDER BY m.movie_id, mf.filename` (deterministic ordering).

comments.note: The original implementation of GetAllMoviesForObfuscationAsync used a correlated subquery (SELECT filename FROM movies_filenames WHERE hash = m.hash ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1) instead of a JOIN. The rewritten INNER JOIN form is semantically cleaner, avoids per-row subquery execution, and matches the intent of the acceptance criteria. No functional regressions in the non-DB test path.

MovieForObfuscation is a positional record; Dapper maps to it via constructor injection by matching column aliases to parameter names case-insensitively. This is implicit and not documented anywhere in the codebase. A brief comment in DapperMovieRepository.cs near this query would help future maintainers avoid accidentally breaking the column alias convention (as was done in GetByIdAsync with the MovieRow private class workaround).

comments.note: AC#3 FAIL — Dapper type-mismatch bug in GetAllMoviesForObfuscationAsync. The implementation calls QueryAsync<MovieForObfuscation> directly. At runtime, MySQL returns m.movie_id as UInt32 (MySqlConnector maps INT UNSIGNED to System.UInt32). Dapper's positional constructor injection looks for a constructor (UInt32 MovieId, String Hash, String CurrentFilename, String OriginalFilename), but MovieForObfuscation has (long MovieId, string Hash, string CurrentFilename, string? OriginalFilename). The types don't match, so Dapper throws InvalidOperationException. Test: GetAllMoviesForObfuscationAsync_ReturnsRowsWithHashAndFilename. Full error: 'A parameterless default constructor or one matching signature (System.UInt32 MovieId, ...) is required for VideoIndexer.Core.Models.MovieForObfuscation materialization'. The existing MovieRow private class in the same file exists specifically for this reason — the Developer did not follow that pattern. Fix: add a private MovieObfuscationRow plain class (property setters, long MovieId) and project to MovieForObfuscation in code, OR cast the SQL column: CAST(m.movie_id AS SIGNED) AS MovieId so MySqlConnector returns Int64.

comments.note: The MovieObfuscationRow workaround (and the original MovieRow) exist because MySqlConnector maps INT UNSIGNED to System.UInt32 while the domain model uses long. This pattern will need to be repeated for any future query that materialises a positional record with a long ID column. Consider documenting this as a project convention in constraints.md, or centralising it via a custom Dapper type handler (SqlMapper.AddTypeHandler) for UInt32→long coercion so future queries can use QueryAsync<T> directly.

DapperMovieRepository.cs now has two private row classes (MovieRow, MovieObfuscationRow) but no consistent naming or placement convention — MovieRow is near the top before the methods, while MovieObfuscationRow is placed inline with its associated method. Movies with no rows in movies_filenames are silently excluded from obfuscation results (INNER JOIN). This is by design — no filename means nothing to obfuscate. NULL OriginalFilename is handled correctly via string? on MovieObfuscationRow.

[documentation-forward] constraints.md documents the MovieRow plain-class workaround but does not mention the MySqlConnector INT UNSIGNED → System.UInt32 vs long type-mismatch that necessitates it at runtime.
